lesson.title: String Positions
lesson.driving_question: How can a program use one position or a short part of a string?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Indexing reads one character and slicing reads a bounded part of a string.
retrieved_knowledge: for and while as prior reading
misconceptions: The slice stop position is not included.
Indexing one character and slicing several characters are different operations.
A position outside the string can cause an IndexError.

blocks.definition: Each character in a string has a numbered position. Python starts counting at position 0.
Indexing reads one character from a string by placing its position in square brackets.
Slicing reads a range of characters with a start position and a stop position separated by a colon.
In a slice, the start is included but the stop position is not included. word[0:3] reads positions 0, 1 and 2.
A small text tool can read an initial and a short preview from the same string, then display both results.
blocks.example:
first = word[0]
preview = word[0:3]
print("Initial:", first, "Preview:", preview)
